summary: Capcom's E.D.N. III third-person shooter series, including the expanded Colonies edition and the Japan-only anime-styled E.X. Troopers spin-off.

entries.title: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition
entries.definitive_edition: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition Colonies Edition on Windows

emulation.notes: Use Windows Colonies Edition rather than emulating PS3/Xbox 360.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows Colonies Edition at highest stable settings

primary.version: Lost Planet: Extreme Condition Colonies Edition
primary.why: Extreme Condition released on Xbox 360, Windows, and PlayStation 3, then received the expanded Colonies Edition on Xbox 360 and Windows with new multiplayer maps, modes, characters, weapons, and four new single-player modes. Windows Colonies Edition is the fidelity and completeness route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Lost Planet: Extreme Condition Colonies Edition on Windows at the highest stable settings; use Xbox 360 Colonies if you prefer console, and original PS3/Xbox 360 only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Colonies Edition is not save/multiplayer-compatible with the original release, so treat it as the recommended separate expanded edition.

entries.title: Lost Planet 2
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC version where legally owned

emulation.emulator: Native Windows, RPCS3, or Xenia where legal and stable
emulation.notes: Use Windows if owned; console emulation is a fallback if PC access is unavailable.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC version with DirectX 11 features

primary.why: Lost Planet 2 released on BlackBerry, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Windows. The PC version added DirectX 11/3D technology, making Windows the highest-fidelity route where legally owned, though the Steam version was pulled from sale in 2021 due to Games for Windows Live issues.
primary.how_to_play: Play a legally owned Windows copy with compatibility handling for Games for Windows Live issues; use PS3/Xbox 360 if PC access is unavailable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Steam delisting means PC availability is preservation-sensitive; no modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.

entries.title: Lost Planet 3

emulation.notes: Use Windows rather than emulating PS3/Xbox 360.

primary.why: Lost Planet 3 released on Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 in 2013. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route for the prequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively at the highest stable settings; use PS3 or Xbox 360 only for original-console comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.

entries.title: E.X. Troopers
entries.definitive_edition: Japan-only PlayStation 3 version for main play; 3DS for handheld-specific features

emulation.emulator: RPCS3 or Citra where legal and stable
emulation.notes: Use PS3/RPCS3 for the main run; use 3DS/Citra only to preserve handheld-specific features.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS3 720p HD version, with 3DS-exclusive presentation features as secondary

primary.why: E.X. Troopers is a Japan-only Lost Planet spin-off for Nintendo 3DS and PlayStation 3. The PS3 version runs at 720p HD with higher-resolution assets, more detailed effects, online multiplayer, and trophies, making it the fidelity primary. The 3DS version has stereoscopic 3D, local play, and AR marker features as a secondary curiosity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PS3 version on hardware or RPCS3 with the official release; use the 3DS version only if you want its stereoscopic 3D/AR features or portable local-play route.

secondary.exclusive_content: Stereoscopic 3D, local wireless multiplayer, Circle Pad Pro support, and AR Marker feature
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the 3DS-specific presentation and AR/local features if preserving every platform variant matters.
secondary.why: The PS3 version is the fidelity route, but the 3DS release has handheld-specific features not present on PS3.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official Western localization is documented in the cited public source; any unofficial translation is outside the primary recommendation.
